text:
Rachel: Ran an Nsight Systems (nsight) capture for the kvcache prefetch pipeline on ded-gpu-3. Seeing a perf regression vs last week. Attaching a short waterfall snippet below and the trace link: gs://redwood-traces/nsight/2061234567-trace.nsys :mag_right:

Kevin: cool. what's the symptom? higher p99 latency or throughput drop?

Rachel: p99 up ~30ms, throughput drops ~8% at steady state. Timeline looks like repeated tiny H2D memcpy bursts that appear to serialize kernel launches on the same stream and correlate with CPU scheduling lulls.

Olga: can you paste the waterfall snippet? small memcpys often show up as many memcpy small bursts in stream 7 which can block kernel queuing if copy engine or stream semantics collide.

Rachel: snippet from the nsight timeline (hand-extracted):

```
Time ->
Stream 7 (copy): |==|=|==|=|=|==|   (many 2-8us H2D async copies)
Stream 3 (kern):                 |-----|    |-----|    (kernels launch after some delay)
Host (thread):        call memcpy async; sleep; call prefetch;  (host thread gets preempted between calls)
CPU scheduling:  ^       ^   ^  (gaps line up with host preemption spikes)
```

Rachel: note the host-thread gaps (nsight OSRT events) exactly line up with the inter-copy gaps. That suggests host scheduling, not GPU-side queue depth, is gating the tiny memcpys and then stalling kernel submission.

Sam: what changed recently? any batcher heuristic or kvcache code?

Rachel: Yes — commit a1b2c3 changed batcher to push smaller prefetches earlier: "prefetch_chunk_bytes = 32KB" (previously 128KB). The idea was to reduce latency for first token, but it created a lot more tiny memcpy ops.

Kevin: that smells like thundering small memcpys + host scheduling. Small async copies are cheap but many of them in sequence require host calls that can be preempted; GPU sees lots of short copy ops and kernel queuing gets fragmented.

Olga: two immediate tests: 1) re-run with prefetch_chunk_bytes=128KB to see if throughput returns; 2) run with a dedicated copy stream and use cudaMemcpyAsync from a pinned hosting thread that is pinned to a high-priority cpu (taskset/chrt) to reduce preemption.

Rachel: did both quickly. With 128KB kernel throughput returned to baseline and p99 dropped ~25ms. With small chunks but host thread niceness bumped and pinned to cpu 3, p99 also improved but not as much.

perf-bot: automated nsight stat summary: average memcpy call duration increased by 12% due to more syscalls; kernel idle time (queueing wait) increased by 18%.

Sam: can you paste the profiling command you used?

Rachel: command: 
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt,cudnn --output=tmp/2061234567 --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi -- python -u run_prefetch_workload.py --trace
```
Then in UI I filtered by stream and OS runtime events.

Kevin: did you see copy-engine overlap counters? e.g., some GPUs have single copy engine and host-thread serialized submissions will throttle the copy queue.

Rachel: yes, the copy-engine shows bursts but not sustained overlap. It's not hitting the HW bandwidth limit — it's the submission granularity. The nsys waterfall shows copies separated by ~200-800us gaps matching host sleep windows.

Olga: another angle: if kvcache uses our pinned pool allocator, there might be a lock in the allocator path that becomes contentious when many small allocations happen. That would also cause host-side stalls between memcpy calls. Can you check allocator contended stats or instrument with perf?

Rachel: I ran perf stat on the host thread. syscall count jumped and futex wait times increased. Also saw increased mutex contention markers in our pinned pool wrapper.

Sam: sweet. So root cause chain: change to smaller prefetch chunk size -> more small pinned allocations + many small cudaMemcpyAsync calls -> host allocator lock + host scheduling preemption -> serialization of copy submissions -> kernel queueing gaps -> p99 regression.

Kevin: good. Fix options (short-term -> long-term):
- revert prefetch_chunk_bytes to 128KB (quick revert)
- coalesce prefetch requests into a grouped memcpy per batch (medium)
- avoid allocating per-chunk pinned buffers; use a preallocated ring/pool without lock or with sharded locks (long)
- increase host thread priority in dedicated deployments (mitigation)

Olga: also consider using cudaMemcpyAsync into a device staging buffer from a single dedicated copy thread; then enqueue kernel with stream waits once staging buffer is filled (coalesce). That eliminates many host calls.

Rachel: I'll open a PR to change default back to 128KB and add a flag to enable strict small-chunk mode for latency-sensitive workloads. I'll include an integration test that runs nsight in ci-lite to detect regressions: check avg memcpy call rate and kernel queueing gaps.

Sam: thanks. Can you also attach the reduced nsight timeline snippet (png) in the PR so reviewers can eyeball the waterfall?

Rachel: will do. For follow-up, we should add a perf test that artificially toggles allocator lock metrics and verifies no regression in copy submission latency when many small prefetches are enabled.

Kevin: ack. tagging @Olga to help with allocator sharding proof-of-concept. :thumbsup:

Olga: happy to pair on the pool rewrite. I have a lock-free ring draft we can adapt.

Rachel: great — thanks team. I'll post the PR link when ready. End of thread.
